JUDGMENT

The legal representatives of the deceased petitioner prosecuted this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act against the respondents by claiming the compensation for the injuries sustained by one Yogesh Chowdhary in a road traffic accident that occurred on 28.09.2020.

2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 28.09.2020 at about 7.20 p.m., the deceased petitioner was riding motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-53- S-6922 on Whitefield main road with slowly and cautiously.

While proceeding near Svastha Hospital took U turn, at that time the driver of the Water Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA-53-D-9259 came from Narayanappa cross road in a rash and negligent manner without following traffic rules and regulations and suddenly took right turn towards Whitefield main road and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle and caused the accident.
Due to the impact, the deceased fell down and sustained injuries.

Immediately after the accident petitioner was shifted to Svastha Hospital, Whitefield, Bengaluru wherein he was admitted as an inpatient and underwent surgery and discharged with an advise of follow-up treatment, restricted fracture movements, not to involve in any strenuous activities.

Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy and he was working as Process Coach- Data at Omega Health Care, Bengaluru and earning Rs.45,000/- per month and deceased was contributing his entire earnings to the maintenance of his family and the deceased was the only earning person of their family and petitioners are dependents upon the income of the deceased.
The petitioners No.1 and 2 are the wife and son of the deceased.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

Hence,
the petitioners prays to award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/-.
3.
After service of notices, both the respondents have appeared before the tribunal through their counsels and filed separate written statements.
The respondent No.1 has filed written statement by contending that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and the same is liable to be dismissed in limine.

He has stated this respondent is having valid driving licence and also valid insurance policy at the time of alleged accident and he has no objection to claim compensation from the respondent No.2 by the petitioner.
On these grounds, prays to dismiss the claim petition against him.

sentences.text: The respondent No.2 insurance company appeared through its advocate and filed its written statement by contending that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and the same is liable to be dismissed in limine.

Further admitted the issuance of policy in favour of the respondent No.1 in respect of Tipper Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AK-486 and the liability of this respondent, if any is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased petitioner.
The respondent No.2 also contended that, the accident is caused by the negligence of the deceased petitioner.
The respondent No.2 has filed additional written statement stating that there is no nexus between cause of death of the deceased and accidental injuries.
On these grounds, prays to dismiss the claim petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.

Whether the petitioner prove that, he sustained grievous injuries in a mo- tor vehicle accident, that was taken place on 28.09.2020 at about 19.20 p.m., when he was proceeding on the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-S- 6922 Whitefield main road, near Svastha Hospital, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Water Tanker bearing Reg. No.KA-53- D-9259 in an actionable negligence?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for ?If so, at what rate and from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
5.
Initially the petition came to be filed by petitioner Yogesh Chowdhary himself by claiming the compensation for the injuries sustained by him.
In support of his case Yogesh Chowdhary himself examined as PW.1 and produced Ex.P1 to P.16 documents in his favour.
Thereafter the PW.1 was fully cross-
examined and the case is posted for further evidence of petitioner.
In that stage the IA under Order 22 Rule 4 is filed by the petitioner No.1(a) and (b) by praying to permit them to come on record in lieu of death of the petitioner Yogesh Chowdhary.
The said IA came to be allowed as per order dated 03.11.2023 in the result the wife and son of Yogesh Chowdhary came on record as Petitioner No.1(a) and (b).
In this regard necessary amendment and amended petition was filed by the petitioner.
Except bringing the petitioner No.1(a) and (b) no other changes are made in the petition.
In the amended petition also the compensation was claimed for the accidental injuries sustained by the petitioner Yogesh Chowdhary in the said accident.
6. In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner Yogesh Chowdhary is examined as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 16.
Further the wife of the said Yogesh Chowdhary examined as PW.2 and produced Ex.P.17 to 20 documents in support of their case.
The respondent No.2 has examined its official as RW.1, and got marked documents at Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2.

sentences.text: Heard the arguments of both sides and perused the material evidence that are available on record.
8. My findings on the above issues are as under.

: R E A S O N S:
Issue No.1:
9.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner Yogesh Chowdhary has filed affidavit in lieu of-examination in-chief, which is considered as P.W.1.

In support of his case, he has produced true copies of FIR, complaint, charge sheet, spot mahazar along with sketch, notice issued to owner of the vehicle and reply issued by him and wound certificate, all these documents are marked under Ex.P.1 to P.6.

In the same way the petitioner No.1(a) i.e., the wife of the Yogesh Chowdhary filed evidence affidavit and produced Ex.P.17 to 20.
10.
As per the documents, the contents of Ex.P.1- FIR and Ex.P2 complaint supports the claim of the petitioners in respect of occurrence of the accident.

The Ex.P.1 FIR registered on the basis of complaint given by one Eshwar Singh who is father-in-law of Yogesh Chowdhary by reporting the accident to the police and also by alleging the rash and negligent driving by the driver of Water Tanker bearing No.KA-53-D-9259.
After registration of the FIR the spot mahazar as per Ex.P.4 was conducted by the I.O. along with rough sketch.

On perusal of the contents of the Ex.P.4 mahazar and the rough sketch Yogesh Chowdhary was proceeding in his motorcycle in the main road and to take right turn when he was coming in the right side portion of the road, the driver of Water Tanker bearing No.KA-53-D-9259 came from left side road and while taking its right turn dashed against the motorcycle of Yogesh Chowdhary.

The copy of IMV report is also available along with Ex.P.3 charge sheet wherein it shows that the right side fuel tank of Water Tanker bearing No.KA-53-D-9259 has got damaged and left side of the motorcycle of Yogesh Chowdhary has got damaged in the said accident.

The said damages mentioned in the IMV report supports the case of the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving by the driver of Water Tanker bearing No.KA-53-D-9259.
11.

The contents of Ex.P4 mahazar and rough sketch along with IMV report establishes that the said Yogesh Chowdhary to take U turn while he was coming in the right side portion of the road the driver of Water Tanker bearing No.KA-53-D-9259 came from left side road in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the left side of the motorcycle of Yogesh Chowdhary.
The contents of Ex.P.3 mahazar and IMV report helped the petitioners to prove their case and alleged negligence by the driver of Water Tanker bearing No.KA-53-D-9259.

sentences.text: The respondent No.1 even though appeared and filed written statement neither choosen to cross- examined the PW.1 and 2 nor lead any evidence to rebut the case of the petitioners.
The respondent No.1 has not choosen to examine the driver of Water Tanker bearing No.KA-53-D-9259 to disprove the case of the petitioners.

13. Wherefore in the absence of any cogent evidence which could rebut the assertions made by PW-1 and 2 on oath supported by Ex.P-3 mahazar and rough sketch along with IMV report, this court should not have any impediment to conclude that the said documents prima-facie suffice to hold that accident, occurred due to actionable negligence on the part of the driver of Water Tanker bearing No.KA-53-D-9259.
14.

It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

entities.text: Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105,
where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the rider of the offending van.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even here in this case the driver of Water Tanker bearing No.KA-53-D-9259 is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part.
Even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the driver of the Water Tanker bearing No.KA-53-D-9259 and he was charge sheeted.
15. By the above said reasons it can be held that there is a negligence on the part of the driver of the Water Tanker bearing No.KA-53-D-9259 was negligent and caused the accident.
16. In the claim petition like the present one strict proof is not necessary but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
All the materials available on record leading to show that, deceased was hale and healthy prior to the accident and after the accident he got injuries.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
17.

This Court has already held Issue No.I in the affirmative which makes it more than obvious that the deceased Yogesh Chowdhary has got injuries in RTA dated 28.09.2020 which is caused by the driver of the Water Tanker bearing No.KA-53-D-9259.
Once the negligence and injuries are proved the next point for consideration is the amount of compensation.

Needless to state the quantum of Yogesh Chowdhary vs Praveen Kumar H.L on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128496002/
5 compensation which is awarded has to be proportionate to the nature of the injuries and the compensation has to be awarded by keeping in mind the pecuniary damages and non-pecuniary damages suffered by the injured-claimant.

sentences.text: 18. Unlike other run of the mill cases, the case at hand has peculiar facts, to the extent that the original claimant died during the pendency of the petition and the petitioners who impleaded themselves claims the compensation.

Except impleading themselves as legal heirs of the deceased petitioner, the petitioners not peladed anything that the death of petitioner Yogesh Chowdhary was due to injuries sustained in the accident.
No nexus between the injury sustained by Yogesh Chowdhary and cause of death of Yogesh Chowdhary is established before this tribunal.

Whether the original claimant was under continuous medication for injuries sustained in the accident and whether he had recovered from the injuries, or not and his death is a result of injuries sustained in the accident is not established before this tribunal.

The petitioners have not taken necessary steps against respondent in criminal case seeking that Section 304-A of IPC be invoked against driver of the offending vehicle nor does it appear that the petitioners got conducted the post-mortem examination of the original petitioner upon his death.

19. It is necessary to note that the injuries were sustained on 28.09.2020 whereas the original claimant demised on 20.08.2023 so there is a gap of 2 years 10 months 23 days between date of accident and date of death.
Further even the PW.2 does not assert that there is nexus between the death of the said Sri. Yogesh Chowdhary and the injuries sustained by him in the accident.
There is no pleading in the amended petition that the death is due to the injuries and there is a nexus between death and injury.

Hence considering the fact that there is a long gap of more than 2 years 10 months between the date of accident and date of death and the said Sri. Yogesh Chowdhary had been discharged from the hospital in the year 2020 itself as per Ex.P7 discharge summary which in turn supported by the fact that PW.2 has nowhere asserted any nexus between the injuries sustained by original claimant in the accident and his death.

Perhaps had the injuries sustained were of such nature that the probable outcome was death, the contention of the petitioners regarding nexus between injuries and death could have been accepted which is not the case here, as the original petitioner, as admitted by PW.2 had been discharged from the hospital and no evidence is available to show that ever since from the date of discharge the original petitioner was consulting doctors and under regular follow up treatment.
20. It is interesting to note that no evidence is made available to show what is the real cause for the death of the original petitioner Sri Yogesh Chowdhary.
Whether original petitioner Yogesh Chowdhary died in the hospital or in the house or what was the actual condition at the time of death is not established before this tribunal.

21. Yet another aspect to be considered is that it is the established principle relating to pleadings and evidence that any amount of evidence without necessary pleading would be futile, similarly, any pleadings no matter how convincing and elaborate, if dispute cannot be accepted by this court, if it is not supported by cogent and reliable evidence.

The reason why this tribunal has emphasized on this principle of law is, as already observed, the petition was filed by the original claimant/ petitioner and he demised during the pendency of the petition, as such, the petitioners impleaded themselves.

sentences.text:
However, having impleaded themselves, the petitioners did not get the petition amended, as such,
there is not even an assertion in the petition to the effect that the original petitioner demised due to injuries sustained in the accident or that there is direct nexus between the death of original petitioner and injuries sustained by him in the accident.
The petitioners did not bother to get the petition amended to include the said contention in their petition.

No doubt, in the petition which was filed originally, the original petitioner had asserted that due to injuries sustained in the accident his life span had reduced, but the point that this tribunal is trying to bring home is that the petitioners should have got the petition amended immediately after their impleading so as to include the said fact in their pleading.

22. To sum up this court finds no hesitation in holding that the petitioners have failed to prove the nexus between death of the original claimant and the injuries sustained by him in the accident, as the petitioners did not get the Postmortem conducted.

Perhaps the Postmortem report would have given this court some material to appreciate the contention of the petitioners, which is not meant to be as the petitioners have not got the Postmortem conducted.

Now that this court has held that the petitioners have failed to prove that there is any nexus between the injuries sustained by the original claimant and his death, the question before this tribunal then what is the fate of this case.
In other words, the question before this court is does the petition seeking compensation for injuries sustained in an RTA abate with the death of the original claimant.

In this regard in Jagannath (Died) By His Lr vs Md. Sabeeuddin rendered on 02.06.2022 and reported in 2022 Latest Caselaw 8042 Kant the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in a similar set of facts, upheld the orders of the tribunal in granting medical expenses even after the death of original claimant during the pendency of the petition.

entities.text: Jagannath (Died) By His Lr vs Md. Sabeeuddin
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in Ningappa Vs The Divisional Controller KSRTC in MFA No.201511/2016 (MV) rendered on on 23 June, 2022 held thus:
7.

entities.text: Ningappa Vs The Divisional Controller KSRTC in MFA No.201511/2016 (MV)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for respondent has placed reliance on a decision of this Court reported in Part-III (2002) ACC 83 (Baburao Sataba Manabutakar Vs. Doreswamy and others) holding that the claimants are not entitled for even medical expenses.

entities.text: Part-III (2002) ACC 83 (Baburao Sataba Manabutakar Vs. Doreswamy and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, the Hon'ble Apex Court in the latest decision in Civil Appeal 4800/2021 arising out of SLP(C) 2873/2021 has held that in view of the death of the deceased/claimant, the legal heirs are entitled for medical expenses, though nexus between the death and injuries is not established.
Under these circumstances, the decision reported in the case of Baburao Sataba Manabutakar (cited supra) is not a good law, in view of the above decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court.
Hence, the claimants are entitled for compensation in respect of medical expenses spent towards treatment of the deceased.
8. On perusal of Ex.P8, it is evident that the deceased was admitted in hospital and around Rs.20,000/- was spent towards medical expenses.
The bill of hospital viz., Vaibhav Medical Center dated 22.02.2014 discloses that more than Rs.16,000/- was paid towards hospital charges.

The other prescriptions are also available and as such, the claimants have spent around Rs.20,000/-
towards medical expenses.

sentences.text: Hence, in view of the above cited decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court, the claimants being the legal heirs of the deceased Ningappa, are entitled for Rs.20,000/- towards medical expenses.

23. Further the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 filed memo with citation MFA 4072/1998 dated 04.09.2001 between Babu Rao Sataba Manabutakar Deceased by his L.Rs V/s Doreswamy &
others wherein it is held as follows 32.

In view of the enormous expenses incurred by the deceased during his hospitalisation as a result of the accident, which will have to be ultimately borned by the legal heirs, I direct the State Government to consider granting ex gratia compensation of Rs. 50,000/- to the appellants.
Hence it is clear that the petitioners are entitled for medical expenses.
(A) TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES:
It is interesting to note that though the PW.1 and 2 both claims that they have spent huge amount towards the medical expenses of the original claimant.
However, when the medical bills exhibited at Ex.P9 series are perused, the sum total of all the bills is Rs.2,35,969/-.
These bills are supported with Ex.P.7 discharge summary and the Ex.P.10 prescriptions.
No serious disputes are made against these bills.

On perusal of the medical records especially the Ex.P6, P7, P9 and P10 which are the wound certificate, discharge summary, medical bills, prescription, make it clear that the petitioner has incurred the medical expenses towards his treatment. which can be rounded off to 2,36,000/-.
Accordingly, the petitioners are entitled for an amount of .2,36,000/- towards medical expenses.
(B) TOWARDS TRANSPORTATION AND OTHER MISCELLANEOUS EXPENSES:

As already observed the Ex.P6 wound certificate and P7 discharge summary makes it amply clear that the original claimant had left foot crush injury and also fracture in left foot bones, for which he underwent treatment as an inpatient from 28.09.2020 to 04.10.2020 and thereafter once again admitted to Svastha Hospital on 21.12.2020 and discharged on same day.
Hence the petitioner might have incurred expenditures for transportation and other miscellaneous expenses.
On consideration of the injuries sustained by the original claimant this Tribunal is of the opinion that it is just and proper to award an amount of .25,000/- under this head.

22. To sum up the above discussion, the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the following :
Towards Medical expenses - . 2,36,000/-
 Towards diet, food, - . 25,000/-
 nourishment, attendant and  conveyance charges  Total - . 2,61,000/-

The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the decision reported in Shriram General Insurance Co.
ltd v. Smt. Laxmi and others rendered in MFA No.103557/2016 rendered on 20.03.2018 awarded interest at the rate of 6% per annum by considering the relevant provisions.

sentences.text: Considering the aforesaid decision and also prevailing Bank rate of interest, this tribunal also deems it proper to award interest at the rate of 6% per annum.

25. LIABILITY:
Now that this court has ascertained the compensation amount, the last aspect of the matter is regarding fixation of liability i.e., who should be made liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner?.
In this regard, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent no.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
In the written statement and also in evidence the RW.1 admitted the existence of policy as per the terms and conditions mentioned therein.
The RW.1 also produced Ex.R.2 copy of policy which was valid from 25.07.2020 to 25.07.2021.
The date of accident is 28.09.2020.

No other grounds are made out by the respondent No.2 insurance company regarding the violation of policy conditions, as such the respondent No.1 and 2 being the owner and insurer are liable to pay the compensation and the respondent No.2 has to indemnify the liability of the respondent No.1 owner alongwith interest at the rate of 6% per annum .
Accordingly this issue is answered in the affirmative.
26. ISSUE No.3:

In view of the reasons assigned in the foregoing paragraphs of this judgment and in view of the finding given on Issue No. 1 and 2, proceeded to pass the following:
"ORDER"
"The claim petition is allowed in part with costs.
Petitioners

are entitled for compensation of .2,61,000/- (Rupees Two lakhs sixty one thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization including interim compensation if any awarded.
The respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners
The respondent No.2 is hereby directed to deposit the compensation amount along with interest within two months from the date of this judgment.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The legal representatives of the deceased petitioner prosecuted this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act against the respondents by claiming the compensation for the injuries sustained by one Yogesh Chowdhary in a road traffic accident that occurred on 28.09.2020.
The respondent No.1 has filed written statement by contending that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and the same is liable to be dismissed in limine.
opennyai_summary.issue:
4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.
Whether the petitioner prove that, he sustained grievous injuries in a mo- tor vehicle accident, that was taken place on 28.09.2020 at about 19.20 p.m., when he was proceeding on the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-S- 6922 Whitefield main road, near Svastha Hospital, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Water Tanker bearing Reg. No.KA-53- D-9259 in an actionable negligence?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for ?If so, at what rate and from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
5.
Now that this court has held that the petitioners have failed to prove that there is any nexus between the injuries sustained by the original claimant and his death, the question before this tribunal then what is the fate of this case.
In other words, the question before this court is does the petition seeking compensation for injuries sustained in an RTA abate with the death of the original claimant.
25. LIABILITY:
Now that this court has ascertained the compensation amount, the last aspect of the matter is regarding fixation of liability i.e., who should be made liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner?.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The respondent No.1 even though appeared and filed written statement neither choosen to cross- examined the PW.1 and 2 nor lead any evidence to rebut the case of the petitioners.
The respondent No.1 has not choosen to examine the driver of Water Tanker bearing No.KA-53-D-9259 to disprove the case of the petitioners.
13. Wherefore in the absence of any cogent evidence which could rebut the assertions made by PW-1 and 2 on oath supported by Ex.P-3 mahazar and rough sketch along with IMV report, this court should not have any impediment to conclude that the said documents prima-facie suffice to hold that accident, occurred due to actionable negligence on the part of the driver of Water Tanker bearing No.KA-53-D-9259.
14.
Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
15. By the above said reasons it can be held that there is a negligence on the part of the driver of the Water Tanker bearing No.KA-53-D-9259 was negligent and caused the accident.
Except impleading themselves as legal heirs of the deceased petitioner, the petitioners not peladed anything that the death of petitioner Yogesh Chowdhary was due to injuries sustained in the accident.
No nexus between the injury sustained by Yogesh Chowdhary and cause of death of Yogesh Chowdhary is established before this tribunal.
Whether the original claimant was under continuous medication for injuries sustained in the accident and whether he had recovered from the injuries, or not and his death is a result of injuries sustained in the accident is not established before this tribunal.
The petitioners have not taken necessary steps against respondent in criminal case seeking that Section 304-A of IPC be invoked against driver of the offending vehicle nor does it appear that the petitioners got conducted the post-mortem examination of the original petitioner upon his death.
19. It is necessary to note that the injuries were sustained on 28.09.2020 whereas the original claimant demised on 20.08.2023 so there is a gap of 2 years 10 months 23 days between date of accident and date of death.
Further even the PW.2 does not assert that there is nexus between the death of the said Sri. Yogesh Chowdhary and the injuries sustained by him in the accident.
There is no pleading in the amended petition that the death is due to the injuries and there is a nexus between death and injury.
Hence considering the fact that there is a long gap of more than 2 years 10 months between the date of accident and date of death and the said Sri. Yogesh Chowdhary had been discharged from the hospital in the year 2020 itself as per Ex.P7 discharge summary which in turn supported by the fact that PW.2 has nowhere asserted any nexus between the injuries sustained by original claimant in the accident and his death.
Perhaps had the injuries sustained were of such nature that the probable outcome was death, the contention of the petitioners regarding nexus between injuries and death could have been accepted which is not the case here, as the original petitioner, as admitted by PW.2 had been discharged from the hospital and no evidence is available to show that ever since from the date of discharge the original petitioner was consulting doctors and under regular follow up treatment.
Whether original petitioner Yogesh Chowdhary died in the hospital or in the house or what was the actual condition at the time of death is not established before this tribunal.
21. Yet another aspect to be considered is that it is the established principle relating to pleadings and evidence that any amount of evidence without necessary pleading would be futile, similarly, any pleadings no matter how convincing and elaborate, if dispute cannot be accepted by this court, if it is not supported by cogent and reliable evidence.
However, having impleaded themselves, the petitioners did not get the petition amended, as such,
there is not even an assertion in the petition to the effect that the original petitioner demised due to injuries sustained in the accident or that there is direct nexus between the death of original petitioner and injuries sustained by him in the accident.
The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the decision reported in Shriram General Insurance Co.
ltd v. Smt. Laxmi and others rendered in MFA No.103557/2016 rendered on 20.03.2018 awarded interest at the rate of 6% per annum by considering the relevant provisions.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.
Learned counsel for respondent has placed reliance on a decision of this Court reported in Part-III (2002) ACC 83 (Baburao Sataba Manabutakar Vs. Doreswamy and others) holding that the claimants are not entitled for even medical expenses.
Hence, the claimants are entitled for compensation in respect of medical expenses spent towards treatment of the deceased.
opennyai_summary.decision:
No serious disputes are made against these bills.
Accordingly, the petitioners are entitled for an amount of .2,36,000/- towards medical expenses.
On consideration of the injuries sustained by the original claimant this Tribunal is of the opinion that it is just and proper to award an amount of .25,000/- under this head.
22. To sum up the above discussion, the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the following :
Towards Medical expenses - . 2,36,000/-
 Towards diet, food, - . 25,000/-
 nourishment, attendant and  conveyance charges  Total - . 2,61,000/-
Totally, the petitioners are entitled compensation of .2,61,000/-.
24.
Accordingly this issue is answered in the affirmative.
26. ISSUE No.3:
In view of the reasons assigned in the foregoing paragraphs of this judgment and in view of the finding given on Issue No. 1 and 2, proceeded to pass the following:
"ORDER"
"The claim petition is allowed in part with costs.
Petitioners
are entitled for compensation of .2,61,000/- (Rupees Two lakhs sixty one thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization including interim compensation if any awarded.
The respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners
The respondent No.2 is hereby directed to deposit the compensation amount along with interest within two months from the date of this judgment.
The petitioners are entitle for the compensation at the ratio of 50:50.
The share of the petitioner by name Nikky Eshwar Singh is directed to be released in her favour by taking necessary documents and vouchers.
The share of the petitioner by name Utkarsh Chowdhary is directed to be deposited in any nationalized bank till he attains the age of majority.
Advocate's fee is fixed at .1,500/-.
Draw award accordingly."
